text:
kaya: Hi team — I'm setting up my CI for the first time and hitting failures when running our GitHub Actions -> Buildkite pipeline. My PR can't trigger the Buildkite job: "Buildkite API returned 403: Forbidden". I tried re-running but same. Any quick checks?

jordan: hey kaya welcome! are you in the org? do you have Write access to repo? 403 from Buildkite usually means the GitHub app doesn't have access to your PR/branch or Buildkite has no pipeline access. pinging @buildkite-bot to see logs.

buildkite-bot: (automated) Received webhook for PR #42. Payload owner = user:kaya. App installation status = user not an org member.

kaya: I am in the org but joined yesterday via invite. Could that be the issue?

ali: yep, sometimes the GitHub App restricts installations to "organization members only" for certain events. Try: go to Settings -> Third-party access on GitHub? Another quick check: can you open Actions tab for the repo and see workflows?

kaya: Actions tab shows 'You don't have access to view workflow runs.'

sophia: that confirms it. Two paths: ask org admin to add you to the team that has "Read" on workflows (org owners), or we can trigger a Buildkite run manually if you need to test.

jordan: @sophia can you add kaya to team ci-engineering? otherwise pinging @people-ops maybe.

sophia: done — added kaya to 'ci-engineering' with repo access. Also updated the GitHub App installation to include user events. Try re-running the PR trigger.

kaya: re-run worked! Buildkite got to the agent step but now the first job fails with: 

```
Run ./scripts/bootstrap.sh
./scripts/bootstrap.sh: line 12: aws: command not found
ERROR: bootstrap failed: missing aws cli
```

ali: Onboarding note: our bootstrap expects aws cli installed in the build image unless you're running on dedicated agents. For first-week devs we usually run the job with the 'local' tag so it picks a dev agent that has aws creds. Are you using the forked repo? PR from fork => won't have secrets or access to protected runners.

kaya: yes it's from my fork. That explains missing creds/secrets. What's the recommended workflow for early devs?

sophia: two options: 1) push a branch to the main repo (we can give you a branch on the repo) or 2) change your pipeline to use the 'allow-forks' test image (not production) — created a short script you can run locally:

```
# temp: run tests locally without secrets
BUILDKITE_AGENT_TAGS=dev-local ./scripts/run-ci-locally.sh
```

jordan: also FYI if you need to debug logs we can run the job with DEBUG=1 and tail the agent logs.

kaya: thanks everyone — super helpful. Two follow ups: who do I ping next time for GH app installs? and is there a short checklist for new hires about CI perms?

ali: ping @sophia or @jordan for org app installs. We'll add a CI onboarding checklist to the devex onboarding doc.

sophia: I'll create a short checklist and drop it in #devex-onboarding.

kaya: awesome, thanks! :raised_hands:
